grants.title: GO8341: Modernised Multicultural Grants Program: Infrastructure for Multicultural Communities
grants.summary: Assessment and notification of outcomes will be divided into 2 batches. The table below identifies the cut-off dates for each batch: Batch 1 - closes 4:00 pm AEST on 18 May 2026 - ID 2025-5201 - Closed Batch 2 - closes 4:00 pm AEDT on 12 November 2026 - ID 2026-6462 - Open. The Australian Government is inviting organisations through an open competitive process to apply to deliver community infrastructure under the Infrastructure for Multicultural Communities program from 2026–27. The Infrastructure for Multicultural Communities grant opportunity provides total funding of up to $41.6 million (GST exclusive) for construction, upgrade or extension of infrastructure. You can apply for one of 3 streams of grant funding based on the type of infrastructure project and amount of grant funding you require for the project. The grant opportunity is comprised of 2 funding opportunities, called batches. You can apply for funding in one batch. Batch 1 opens on 7 April 2026 and closes on 18 May 2026. Batch 2 opens on 18 May 2026 and closes on 12 November 2026. The following groups and projects will be prioritised for funding: new and emerging multicultural communities, as defined below projects focussed on achieving positive outcomes for multicultural women, multicultural LGBTIQA+ community members, and multicultural people with a disability. Co-contributions are required towards the value of your project and the minimum amount of co funding is determined by whether you are applying as a priority group/project or other. A recording of an information session held earlier this year for this grant opportunity can be found by visiting Infrastructure for Multicultural Grant – 6 May 2026 Information Session - Meeting Recording.

grants.title: GO8220: Saluting their Service Commemorative Grants Program 2026–27
grants.summary: Assessment and notification of outcomes will be into 2 batches. The table below identifies the cut-off dates for all 2 batches: Batch 1 - closes 9:00 PM AEST on 29 July 2026 - ID 2025-5415 - Closed Batch 2 - closes 9:00 PM AEDT 21 January 2027 - ID 2025-5416 - Open. The Australian Government is inviting eligible organisations to apply for grant funding under the Saluting Their Service Commemorative Grants Program (STS program). The objective of the STS Program is to commemorate the service and sacrifice of Australia’s service personnel who served in wars, conflicts and peace operations, including National Service personnel, and their families. The intended outcome of the STS Program is to provide funding for projects and activities that: promote appreciation and understanding of the experiences of service, and the role of service personnel preserve, add to the sum of knowledge on, or provide access to information about Australia’s wartime heritage. 1. Community Grants Grants up to $10,000 are available for projects and activities that: are focused on the local community commemorate the service and sacrifice of local community members are primarily accessed by the local community. 2. Major Grants Grants between $10,001 and $150,000 are available for major commemorative projects and activities that are significant from a national, state, territory and/or broader regional perspective. These projects may include the construction of new war or peace memorials where none currently exist, as well as additions to existing memorials. If your project relates to restoring or changing a memorial or other commemorative artefact, there may be heritage and conservation considerations.

grants.title: GO8681: NIEA Expression of Interest for funding commencing in 2027
grants.summary: The Office of National Intelligence (ONI) is conducting an Expression of Interest (EOI) grant opportunity for the National Intelligence Explore Award (NIEA). The National Intelligence Community (NIC) Research Program enables the Australian academic community to undertake competitive, unclassified research into NIC research priorities. The program supports peer-reviewed research that deepens understanding of emerging science, social science, engineering and technology. NIC innovation is facilitated through the creation of sovereign expertise, discovery of new insights and development of an R&D ecosystem to underpin emerging technological capability. A NIEA (up to 12 available) provides up to $750k over three years to enable research into NIC research priorities and challenges. The NIEA will be awarded to early-mid career researchers partnering with experienced researchers and emerging PhD candidates. The NIEA will also enable the possibility for extension research. Research proposals are invited to address an Intelligence Science and Technology Challenge or a NIC-defined Research Topic. Two-stage Application Process 1. Expression of Interest (EOIs) applications open: 2 November 2026 close: 10 December 2026 2. Full applications by invitation only open: 21 December 2026 close: 3 March 2027 It is strongly recommended that you read the Grant Guidelines carefully to ensure your eligibility before applying.

grants.title: GO8700: Forestry Industry - Support Plantation Establishment Round 4
grants.summary: Assessment and notification of outcomes will be divided into 2 batches. The table below identifies the cut-off dates for the 2 batches: Batch 1 - closes 4:00 pm AEDT on 16 December 2026 - ID 2026-6698 - Open Batch 2 - closes 4:00 pm AEST on 30 June 2027 - ID 2026-7196 - Closed. The Australian Government is inviting organisations via a Demand Driven (eligibility based) process to deliver services under the Forestry Industry - Support Plantation Establishment Program. Round 4 of the program will contribute to the Forestry Growth Fund, helping to grow Australia’s forestry industry by supporting regional jobs and rural communities, innovation, sustainable fibre supply, and domestic capacity to product high-value wood products for housing and construction. The objectives of the program are to: increase future plantation forest resources available for processing, as well as for plantation forest management, harvesting and haulage employment support private industry, First Nations businesses, farm foresters and state and territory forestry bodies to expand the Australian plantation forest estate contribute to meeting Australia’s carbon emission reduction targets, including under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, and the Kyoto Protocol to the Climate Change Convention. At the time of submitting your application, you must not have planted the trees as part of your project activities. You also can not include any activities that have or will be undertaken prior to the earliest activity start date for the relevant batch you are applying to as part of your grant funded or co-contribution activities. The earliest activity start dates for each batch are: Batch 1: May 2027 Batch 2: November 2027.

grants.title: GO8631: Veteran Wellbeing Grants (VWG) Program 2026-27
grants.summary: The Australian Government is providing funding under the VWG Program through a Targeted Competitive grants process. To be eligible to apply your organisation must be either: an ESO applying in its own right (as defined in the Grant Opportunity Guidelines), or as the lead organisation of a consortium, or a non-ESO applying as the lead member of a consortium with at least one ESO and be one of the legal entity types as outlined in the Grant Opportunity Guidelines. The Australian Government has announced a total of up to $3.744 million (GST exclusive) for the VWG Program for the 2026–27 financial year. Applications will be considered under 2 grant streams: Stream A Small Grants (up to a maximum of $50,000 per grant) and Stream B Large Grants (from $50,001 to a maximum of $200,000 per grant). There is no set proportion of the funding allocated per stream. The objectives of the VWG Program are to: maintain and improve the independence and quality of life of members of the veteran community, by providing funding for activities and projects that sustain or enhance health and social wellbeing deliver activities and projects not already provided by Australian, state, territory or local government funding to the veteran community to build future community capacity expand on existing activities and projects offered to the veteran community in new regions within Australia or in the development of new activities and projects that will be offered in more than one location raise awareness of the important issues faced by the veteran community.

grants.title: GO8669: Volunteer Management Activity - 2027-2031
grants.summary: The Australian Government is inviting Volunteering Australia via a restricted process to apply to deliver services under the Family and Communities Program, Volunteer Management Activity nationally from 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2031. The grant will contribute to Program 2.1.6: Volunteering and Community Connectedness under DSS Outcome 2 by funding a nationally coordinated model led by Volunteering Australia, supported by state and territory peak bodies, and targeted legal and capacity-building services. The grant opportunity is intended to strengthen community connectedness, improve inclusion and accessibility in volunteering. Funding will support the delivery of training, resources, tools, information and advisory services for volunteers and Volunteer Involving Organisations (VIOs), as well as targeted legal and capacity-building assistance. The activity will also support improved volunteer management practices, increased participation in volunteering, and greater inclusion and accessibility for diverse communities. The VMA aligns with the National Strategy for Volunteering 2023–2033 and aims to strengthen community connectedness, build organisational capability, and create a volunteering ecosystem that is responsive to the changing needs of volunteers, organisations and communities.

grants.title: GO8372: MRFF – Indigenous Health Research Fund – 2026 Empowering Community-Controlled Research Grant Opportunity
grants.summary: The Medical Research Future Fund (MRFF) Indigenous Health Research Fund aims to improve the health of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people through: Indigenous-led research practice and governance knowledge translation evidence-based structural change in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health practice building on the unique knowledge, strengths and endurance of our communities, with particular reference to Country, culture and spirituality The objective of this grant opportunity is to provide a grant of financial assistance to an organisation or consortium to run an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Community-Controlled program to support Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander led health and medical research projects. The successful applicant is required to undertake a review, develop a Strategic Priorities Investment Plan and partner with and support Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health and medical research projects and researchers. This grant opportunity is being administered by NHMRC on behalf of the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing. Further information on the Medical Research Future Fund is available from the Department of Health, Disability and Ageing's website. A list of Eligible Organisations can be found on the NHMRC List of MRFF Eligible Organisations webpage.

grants.title: GO8163: Partnership Projects 2026
grants.summary: Partnership Projects will support collaborations, within the Australian context, that translate research evidence into health policy and health practice, to improve health services and processes. The objectives of the Partnership Project scheme are to: • Meet the need for more effective integration of research evidence into health policy and service delivery • Create partnerships among policy makers, managers, service providers and researchers • Provide support to answer often complex and difficult questions that policy makers, managers and service providers face when making decisions and implementing policies that affect Australians’ health and health care • Be highly responsive to the priorities of government, the community and health professionals • Enable applicants to apply for funding at any time during the year to allow researchers and Partner Organisations to develop timely collaborations.

grants.title: GO8677: Alcohol and Other Drugs (AOD) Peak Organisations
grants.summary: This closed non-competitive grant opportunity will provide funding to Alcohol and Other Drug (AOD) Peak Organisations to strengthen sector leadership, capacity building and advocacy, while also enhancing national data capability through improved data collection, analysis, evaluation and reporting. The objectives of the grant opportunity are to: • improve national alignment and consistency in AOD data collection, reporting, and performance monitoring in line with the National Drug Strategy and relevant national frameworks • strengthen organisational and workforce capability across the sector • support evidence-based decision-making by increasing access, reliability, and usefulness of data for service providers, policymakers, and stakeholders • support workforce development and training, including cultural safety and embedding a lived experience (peer) workforce • support program data collection and management • enable services to leverage digital infrastructure to support connected care • commission and disseminate research and data to inform policy and monitor emerging trends and issues, and • improve cross-system partnerships and governance, including representation from people with lived experience. Note: Please see updated Grant Opportunity Guidelines published on 4 November 2026. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8650: Distinguished Fellow for Prevention and Early Intervention in Child Health
grants.summary: The Distinguished Fellow for Prevention and Early Intervention in Child Health grant opportunity aims to establish national leadership in prevention and early intervention research across child health through an investment of $5 million over five years (from 2026-27). The investment will provide leadership to support medical research into prevalent childhood conditions including obesity, cardiovascular disease, mental health conditions and disability. The grant will support the Distinguished Fellow position, Postdoctoral Fellows, Research Assistants, PhD Scholarships and associated research costs, to strengthen Australia’s capacity to generate and translate evidence that improves the health and wellbeing of children and young people. This opportunity aligns with the Intergenerational Report 2023 and National Preventative Health Strategy (2021-30) and the Government's commitment to improve health outcomes through prevention, early intervention, and evidence-based research for Australian Children. The grant opportunity will establish national leadership to advance research and translation in prevention and early intervention across these priority areas. Aims to support innovative, evidence-based approaches that reduce disease burden, improve long-term outcomes, and contribute to a more sustainable health system. The grant opportunity will also support research that addresses the prevention and early intervention needs of priority child and youth population groups who experience inequities in health outcomes. This includes Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children and young people, children and young people living in remote or rural communities, children with disability (including intellectual disability), children from culturally and linguistically diverse communities (including immigrants and refugees), and LGBTIQ+ children. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8674: National Support for Child and Youth Mental Health Program
grants.summary: This grant opportunity was initiated through the Australian Government Response to the National Mental Health Commission’s Review of Mental Health Programs and Services. The Review raised a number of issues around the delivery of child mental health programs and suggested particular benefit in bundling measures to provide more comprehensive, targeted, and integrated services and supports for this vulnerable population group. In response, the Australian Government announced it would work across portfolios to join up support for child mental health, commencing with the early years and going through to adolescence. This Grant Opportunity consists of 2 streams: • Stream 1: National Workforce Support in Child Mental Health initiative (National Workforce Centre for Child Mental Health) • Stream 2: Mental Health in Education initiative (Be You). Stream 1: National Workforce Support in Child Mental Health initiative (National Workforce Centre for Child Mental Health) This stream will provide funding of up to $32 million over four years for Emerging Minds to continue to deliver the National Workforce Centre for Child Mental Health from 1 July 2027 to 30 June 2031. Stream 2: Mental Health in Education initiative (Be You) This stream will provide funding of up to $92 million over four years for Beyond Blue to continue to deliver Be You from 1 July 2027 to 30 June 2031. Under Program 1.2: Mental Health and Suicide Prevention, the Australian Government is committed to improving the mental health and wellbeing of all Australians, including a focus on suicide prevention. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8637: Accelerating Electric Vehicle Charging Program
grants.summary: The Australian Government is inviting organisations via a restricted process to apply to deliver a grant under Accelerating Electric Vehicle Charging Program. For this Grant, $33.2 million GST exclusive is available over the 2027–28 and 2028–29 financial years. Grant activities must be completed by 30 April 2029. The Accelerating Electric Vehicle Charging Program seeks to leverage the complementary strengths of Distribution Network Service Providers (DNSPs) and Charge Point Operators (CPOs) to rapidly rollout electric vehicle (EV) chargers and support the creation of a dynamic market that can meet the future needs of Australian EV drivers. The deployment of EV chargers and electrification of light vehicles is a key part of the Australian Government’s plan to rapidly decarbonise the transport sector and meet emissions reduction targets. The objectives of this program are to: support emissions reduction in the transport sector to help meet net zero targets by building confidence in Australia’s public EV charging network and supporting Australians with their choice to purchase an EV accelerate the deployment of EV chargers by leveraging the complementary strengths of DNSPs and CPOs to reduce the time and cost to connect preserve competition while filling gaps in the public EV charging network, targeting the deployment of: kerbside EV chargers that offer affordable charging for Australians without access to home-charging; and EV chargers in regional blackspots that support journeys and regional communities. To view key program documents please create a login before clicking on the ‘Grant Opportunity Documents’ button in the left-hand pane.

grants.title: GO8502: Support at Home Thin Markets 2026-27 (Round 3)
grants.summary: The Support at Home Thin Markets 2026-27 (Round 3) Grant Opportunity provides flexible funding to eligible Support at Home providers that deliver aged care services in thin markets. This grant opportunity is the third funding round under the Support at Home Thin Markets Grant program. Providers that received funding in Round 1 (GO7600) and/or Round 2 (GO7988) may also apply in Round 3. Providers that deliver rural and remote services in Modified Monash areas 3 to 7, or that deliver specialised services in any region, may be eligible to apply. This grant opportunity has two streams: • Stream One: Rural, remote and specialised services • Stream Two: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander services. Providers may apply for either Stream One OR Stream Two. Some grant applicants may require a valid Specialisation Verification for aged care services. As gathering the necessary documents can be time consuming, we encourage applicants to plan ahead. Note: Please see updated Frequently Asked Questions - Version 2 - published on 9 September 2026. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8696: Indigenous Visual Arts Industry Support program, Closed Non-Competitive Grant Round 2027
grants.summary: Funding will be provided to organisations for activities that best contribute to delivery of the following Program outcomes: a professional, viable and ethical Indigenous visual arts industry that features strong participation by, and provides economic opportunities for, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people the continued production, exhibition, critique, purchase and collection of Indigenous visual art.

grants.title: GO8697: Indigenous Visual Arts Industry Support program, Open Competitive Grant Round 2027
grants.summary: Funding will be provided to organisations for activities that best contribute to delivery of the following Program outcomes: a professional, viable and ethical Indigenous visual arts industry that features strong participation by, and provides economic opportunities for, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people the continued production, exhibition, critique, purchase and collection of Indigenous visual art.

grants.title: GO8662: 2026-27 Marking (First World War) Private Graves Grants Program
grants.summary: Throughout Australia, individuals and groups are working to identify private unmarked graves of First World War veterans and marking these graves to recognise their service. This Marking (First World War) Private Graves Grants (MPG) Program contributes to the cost of establishing a grave marker on currently unmarked private graves. The MPG Program provides one-off funding of up to $620 per grave to assist with the purchase of a grave marker for unmarked private graves of veterans of the First World War. You can seek funding for up to 10 grave markers in each individual application, and you may only submit a maximum of 2 applications. The objective of the grant opportunity is to contribute to community recognition of the service and sacrifice of service personnel in the First World War. It does this by providing funding to contribute to the cost of establishing a grave marker on currently unmarked private graves. The intended outcome of the MPG Program is to mark private graves of veterans of the First World War so as to: enable community recognition of service preserve and add to the knowledge of, or provide information about, Australia’s wartime heritage.

grants.title: GO8642: Indigenous Ranger Biosecurity Program - Ranger Capability Building Grants - Round 4
grants.summary: The Australian Government is inviting applications from Indigenous Ranger organisations with current fee-for-service contracts with the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (the department), via a restricted process, to apply for a grant under the Ranger Capability Building Grants Program, Round 4. For this grant, $5 million (GST exclusive) is available over the 2026–27 and 2027–28 financial years. Grant agreements will be up to 2 years in length. The Indigenous Ranger Biosecurity Program helps protect Australia’s $100 billion agriculture industries by partnering with Indigenous Rangers to provide vital surveillance needed for the early detection of biosecurity threats across northern Australia. The intended outcomes of the grant program are: Increased capacity of Indigenous Rangers to undertake current and future biosecurity fee-for-service activities for the department. Improved quality of biosecurity surveillance data and reporting. Increased community awareness of high-risk pests and diseases. Improved work health and safety for Indigenous Rangers in remote areas. Increased skills and capability of Indigenous Rangers to enhance their career pathways. Create a career pathway for Rangers with specialist skills in biosecurity. Facilitate Indigenous-led leadership, mentoring and training for rangers in pests and diseases and surveillance technique. Support achievement of place-based biosecurity objectives of traditional owners. Assist in integration of traditional First Nations environmental practices into biosecurity monitoring and surveillance.

grants.title: GO8646: Schools Pathways Program Round 2
grants.summary: The grant opportunity is for an organisation to deliver a project which: facilitates an understanding of the defence industry provides access to defence industry career experiences, mentoring and networking opportunities, and encourages student participation in STEM activities and/or subjects. Projects under the grant opportunity can have national reach or specifically target the workforce needs of one or more critical defence industry hubs, such as the Hunter region of NSW, Cairns in North Queensland, and Edinburgh in South Australia.
